defect: Earth's north pole is 'polo' (Hilagang Polo); 'poste' means a post/pillar like an electric post.
tl: Ang Polaris o 'North Star' ay tila hindi gumagalaw sa langit dahil halos nasa direksyon ito ng hilagang poste ng Earth! Ginagamit ito ng mga manlalakbay para malaman ang direksyong hilaga.
en: Polaris, the 'North Star,' seems to stay still in the sky because it's almost above Earth's north pole! Travelers use it to find the direction north.

defect: Magnetic poles are 'polo' in Filipino science; 'poste' means a physical post, so the field lines appear to run post-to-post.
tl:
Ano ang binubuo ng magnetic field ng Daigdig?

Mga di-nakikitang linya! Umaabot ang mga ito mula sa isang poste papunta sa kabila.
en:
What is Earth's magnetic field made of?

It's made of invisible lines! They run all the way from one pole to the other.

defect: Magnet poles are 'polo'; 'poste' means post/pillar, so 'magkaparehong poste ng magnet' reads as identical posts, not like poles.
tl: Ang magkaparehong poste ng dalawang magnet ay nagtataboy, pero ang magkasalungat na poste ay nag-aakit sa isa't isa!
en: Like poles of two magnets push each other away, but opposite poles pull toward each other like magic!

defect: 'Like poles' should be 'magkaparehong polo'; 'poste' means a physical post.
tl: Kapag pinagdikit mo ang dalawang magkaparehong poste, nagtataboy o nag-iiwasan ang mga ito!
en: When you put two like poles together, they push apart and repel each other!

defect: 'Opposite poles' should be 'magkasalungat na polo'; 'poste' means a post/pillar.
tl:
Ano ang nangyayari kapag nagkaharap ang magkasalungat na poste?

Ang magkasalungat na poste, tulad ng hilaga at timog, ay umaakit at dumidikit sa isa't isa!
en:
What happens when opposite poles meet?

Opposite poles, like north and south, attract and stick to each other!

defect: A magnet's two poles are its 'polo'; 'poste' means posts, so the answer says the force is strongest at its two posts.
tl:
Saan pinakamalakas ang puwersa ng magnet?

Pinakamalakas ang puwersa ng magnet sa dalawang poste niyan, at mas mahina sa gitna.
en:
Where is a magnet's force the strongest?

A magnet's force is strongest at its two poles and weaker in the middle.

defect: Magnet poles are 'polo'; 'poste' means physical posts.
tl:
Ano ang nangyayari kapag nagtatagpo ang mga poste ng magnet?

Magkasalungat na poste ng magnet ay naghihilahan, ngunit magkaparehong poste ay nagtutulakan! Hilaga at timog, magkaakit!
en:
What happens when magnet poles meet?

Opposite magnet poles pull together, but like poles push apart! North and south attract, but north and north repel!

defect: Like magnetic poles = 'magkatulad na polo'; 'poste' means posts, which makes the maglev explanation incoherent.
tl:
Bakit lumulutang at napakabilis ng maglev train?

Ang magkatulad na poste ng magnet ay nagtutulakan, kaya lumulutang ito sa riles nang halos walang friction!
en:
Why does a maglev train float and go so fast?

Like magnetic poles push apart, so it floats above the track with almost no friction!

defect: The horseshoe magnet's ends are 'polo', not 'poste' (posts).
tl:
Bakit sobrang lakas ng horseshoe magnet?

Hugis-U ito na may dalawang poste sa dulo, kaya mas malakas humila ng bakal kaysa tuwid na magnet!
en:
Why is a horseshoe magnet so strong?

It's U-shaped with poles at both ends, letting it pull iron much stronger than a straight bar magnet!

defect: Earth's poles are 'polo'; 'malapit sa mga poste' says the glow happens near posts/pillars.
tl:
Ano ang nagdudulot ng makukulay na aurora sa langit?

Ang Araw! Kapag tumama ang mga particle mula sa solar wind sa hangin sa itaas ng Mundo malapit sa mga poste, nagliliwanag ito at nagiging makukulay na ilaw.
en:
What causes the beautiful, colorful auroras in the sky?

The Sun! When solar wind particles hit the air high above Earth near the poles, the air glows and turns into colorful lights.

defect: Earth's two poles are 'polo', not 'poste' (posts), so the aurora location and magnetic guiding are garbled.
tl: Nakikita lang ang aurora malapit sa magkabilang poste ng Mundo, hindi sa tropikal na lugar tulad ng Pilipinas. Ginagabayan ng magnetikong puwersa ng Mundo ang mga particle ng Araw patungo sa mga poste!
en: Auroras are seen only near Earth's two poles, not in tropical places like the Philippines. Earth's magnetic force guides the Sun's particles toward the poles!

defect: Opposite magnetic poles = 'magkasalungat na polo'; 'poste' means post/pillar.
tl: Ang magkasalungat na poste ng magneto ay naghihilahan! Pero kung magkapareho, sila ay nagtataboy.
en: Opposite magnetic poles attract each other like magic! But if they are the same, they push away.

defect: Mars's polar caps sit at its 'polo'; 'dalawang poste nito' says two posts.
tl: May mga takip na yelo ang Mars sa dalawang poste nito, gawa sa tubig at frozen carbon dioxide!
en: Mars has cool icy caps at both poles, made of water ice and frozen carbon dioxide!

defect: 'Mas malamig sa mga poste' says it is colder at the posts; Earth's poles are 'polo'.
tl: Bilog ang Earth, kaya mas mainit sa ekwador at mas malamig sa mga poste! Direktang tumatama ang sinag sa ekwador, pero pahilis sa mga poste kaya mas mahina ang init.
en: The Earth is round, making the equator hotter and the poles colder! Sunlight strikes directly at the equator, but slants at the poles, making the warmth weaker.

defect: Both the magnetic poles and the true North/South Poles are rendered as 'poste' (posts) instead of 'polo'.
suggested: polo (Hilagang Polo at Timog na Polo)
tl:
Nasa eksaktong lugar ba ang mga magnetikong poste ng Daigdig tulad ng tunay na Hilaga at Timog na Poste?

Hindi! Ang mga magnetikong poste na tinuturo ng kompas ay hindi eksaktong nasa parehong lugar ng tunay na Hilaga at Timog na Poste ng pag-ikot ng Daigdig.
en:
Are Earth's magnetic poles in the exact same spot as the true North and South Poles?

Nope! The magnetic poles where your compass points aren't in the exact same spot as the true North and South Poles of Earth's spin.

defect: Earth's magnetic poles are 'polo'; 'magnetikong poste' means a magnetic post.
tl: Ang magnetikong poste ng Daigdig ay dahan-dahang gumagalaw! Sa napakahabang panahon, ang buong magnetikong larangan ay nakapagpapalit pa ng direksyon!
en: Earth's magnetic poles slowly wander over time! Over very long ages, the whole magnetic field can even flip and reverse direction!

defect: latian means swamp/marsh (a permanent wetland), not a rain puddle; 'swamps in a schoolyard' is a different thing entirely and cannot dry up in a day
tl: Nawawala ang mga latian sa bakuran ng paaralan sa Quezon City tuwing maaraw dahil ang likidong tubig ay nag-e-evaporate at nagiging hindi nakikitang gas!
en: Puddles in a Quezon City schoolyard disappear on sunny days because the liquid water evaporates into an invisible gas!

defect: latian = swamp/marsh, not puddle; the card is about small temporary pools drying up, not wetlands
tl: Natutuyo ang mga latian dahil ang tubig ay nag-e-evaporate at nagiging gas sa temperatura ng silid, kaya hindi kailangang umabot sa boiling point!
en: Puddles dry up because water evaporates into a gas at room temperature, so it doesn't need to reach a boiling point!

defect: 'rain puddles' rendered as latian (swamp/marsh); the question becomes about wetlands, a different entity
suggested: mga natipong tubig ng ulan / mga lusak
tl:
Bakit natutuyo ang mga latian kahit hindi kumukulo?

Nag-e-evaporate ang tubig at nagiging invisible na water vapor sa room temperature, bago pa man umabot sa boiling point!
en:
Why do rain puddles dry up without boiling?

Liquid water evaporates into invisible water vapor at room temperature, long before reaching its boiling point!

defect: puddles translated as latian (swamp/marsh) — wrong entity for the water-cycle example of small pools evaporating
tl: Nag-e-evaporate ang sikat ng araw sa tubig mula sa dagat at latian! Nagsisimula ito ng water cycle na nagdadala ng ulan sa bukirin at gubat.
en: Sunlight evaporates water from seas and puddles! This starts the water cycle, which later brings rain to our farms and forests.

defect: "tihik" is not a sea urchin (tihik = kuripot/maramot, a stingy person); the Tagalog never names the animal, so the child is told a miser can move its spines.
tl:
Kaya ba ng tihik na igalaw ang mga tinik nito?

Oo! Hindi nakatutok lang ang mga tinik nito — kayang itutok ng tihik ang mga ito sa anumang humihipo dito bilang pananggalang.
en:
Can a sea urchin actually move its spines?

Yes! Its spines aren't fixed — the sea urchin can point them toward anything that touches it, as a defense.

defect: "tihik" means stingy/miserly, not sea urchin — the Tagalog warns about stepping on a miser, and the animal is never named.
tl: Kapag natapakan mo nang nakayapak ang tihik, masakit ito dahil matutulis ang tinik nito — kaya mag-ingat sa batuhang dagat.
en: Stepping barefoot on a sea urchin can be painful — its sharp spines can prick your foot, so be careful on rocky seashores.

defect: "tihik" (stingy person) is not the sea urchin; the child learns starfish are related to a non-animal word instead of the echinoderm.
tl: Magkamag-anak pala ang starfish at ang tihik — parehong kabilang sila sa grupo ng mga hayop-dagat na may matinik na balat, ang echinoderm.
en: The starfish and the sea urchin are actually relatives — both belong to a group of spiny-skinned sea animals called echinoderms.

defect: "tihik" means stingy/kuripot, not sea urchin; the Tagalog card describes tube feet on an animal that is never actually named.
tl: Ang tihik ay gumagalaw gamit ang maliliit na paang puno ng tubig na lumalabas sa pagitan ng mga tinik nito, at ginagamit din nito ang mga ito para kumapit sa bato.
en: A sea urchin moves using tiny water-filled tube feet poking out between its spines — it also uses them to grip onto rocks.

defect: "tihik" is not the Tagalog for sea urchin (it means stingy), so the 'test' shell is attributed to a nonexistent animal.
tl: Sa ilalim ng mga tinik ng tihik ay may matigas at bilog na balat na tinatawag na 'test'. Ito ang naiiwan kapag namatay na ito at nalaglag ang mga tinik.
en: Beneath its spines, a sea urchin has a hard round shell called a 'test'. This is what's left after the animal dies and its spines fall off.

defect: Hooke's law is about a coil spring, but "bukal" is a water spring/fountain — the Tagalog says you stretch a spring of water; every other "bukal" in this bank is a water spring.
tl: Sabi ng Batas ni Hooke: habang mas malayo ang pagkaunat mo sa isang bukal (spring), mas malakas ang puwersa nito pabalik! F = kx iyon.
en: Hooke's law says: the farther you stretch a spring, the stronger its pull-back force! That's F = kx.

defect: "sustansya" means nutrient/nourishment, not substance — the Tagalog defines chlorophyll as the green NUTRIENT in leaves; the bank elsewhere uses "sangkap" for substance.
tl:
Ano ang chlorophyll?

Ang chlorophyll ang berdeng sustansya sa dahon na sumisipsip ng enerhiya mula sa araw para magamit sa potosintesis.
en:
What is chlorophyll?

Chlorophyll is the green substance in leaves that absorbs energy from sunlight to use in photosynthesis.

defect: '200 araw ng bagyo bawat taon' reads as 200 TYPHOON days a year, which is false; the card is about thunderstorm/lightning days
suggested: kulog-bagyo (e.g. '200 araw na may kulog at kidlat')
tl: Nakakaranas ang Pilipinas ng mga 200 araw ng bagyo bawat taon! Ang tropical climate, mataas na humidity, at mainit na dagat ay nagdudulot ng madalas na kidlat at kulog.
en: The Philippines gets about 200 thunderstorm days a year! Our tropical climate, high humidity, and warm seas make lightning and thunder very frequent.

defect: bakulaw means gorilla/ape, not toad — the whole card then describes the wrong animal
tl: Ang mga bakulaw ay may tuyo at kulubot na balat at karaniwang nasa lupa, hindi tulad ng makinis at tubig-tubig na mga palaka.
en: Toads have dry, bumpy skin and live mostly on land, unlike smooth, water-loving frogs.

defect: 'batuhan ng lubid' means throwing ropes at each other; tug-of-war is a pulling game
tl: Sa masayang laro ng batuhan ng lubid, panalo ang panig na mas malakas humila sa lubid!
en: In a fun game of tug-of-war, the side that pulls the rope harder wins!
